ml.model.linear_regression.name: Linear regression
ml.model.linear_regression.description: A weighted sum of the features: fast, and every weight can be read.
ml.model.huber.name: Huber regression
ml.model.huber.description: A linear model that gives less weight to extreme errors.
ml.model.quantile.name: Quantile regression
ml.model.quantile.description: Predicts the median (or another percentile) instead of the mean.
ml.model.bayesian_ridge.name: Bayesian ridge
ml.model.bayesian_ridge.description: A ridge regression whose penalty is learnt from the data, with uncertainty on the weights.
ml.model.ard.name: ARD regression
ml.model.ard.description: Bayesian regression that switches off useless features by itself.
ml.model.glm_poisson.name: Poisson regression
ml.model.glm_poisson.description: For counts (≥ 0): the log of the expected count is linear in the features.
ml.model.glm_gamma.name: Gamma regression
ml.model.glm_gamma.description: For positive amounts whose spread grows with their size.
ml.model.glm_tweedie.name: Tweedie regression
ml.model.glm_tweedie.description: For amounts with many exact zeros (claims, sales).
ml.model.logistic_regression.name: Logistic regression
ml.model.logistic_regression.description: A weighted sum of the features turned into a probability: fast and interpretable.
ml.model.ridge_classifier.name: Ridge classifier
ml.model.ridge_classifier.description: A ridge regression on the classes: very fast.
ml.model.perceptron.name: Perceptron
ml.model.perceptron.description: The simplest neural unit: a linear frontier learnt by corrections.
ml.model.passive_aggressive.name: Passive-aggressive
ml.model.passive_aggressive.description: Updates only when wrong, by just enough to be right: for large or streaming data.
ml.model.sgd.name: SGD (stochastic gradient descent)
ml.model.sgd.description: A linear model fitted a few rows at a time: made for large data.
ml.model.lda.name: Linear discriminant analysis
ml.model.lda.description: Each class as a bell shape with a shared spread: a linear frontier.
ml.model.qda.name: Quadratic discriminant analysis
ml.model.qda.description: Each class as a bell shape with its own spread: curved frontiers.
ml.model.knn.name: k-nearest neighbours
ml.model.knn.description: Predicts like the k most similar rows.
ml.model.linear_svm.name: Linear SVM
ml.model.linear_svm.description: The widest straight frontier between classes (or a tube around the numbers).
ml.model.kernel_svm.name: Kernel SVM
ml.model.kernel_svm.description: A frontier that bends through a kernel: powerful on small and medium data.
ml.model.nu_svm.name: Nu-SVM
ml.model.nu_svm.description: A kernel SVM set by the share of support vectors instead of C.
ml.model.radius_neighbours.name: Radius neighbours
ml.model.radius_neighbours.description: Predicts like every row within a given distance (not a fixed number of neighbours).
ml.model.categorical_nb.name: Categorical Naive Bayes
ml.model.categorical_nb.description: Counts how often each category (numbers cut into bins) appears in each class.
ml.model.gaussian_nb.name: Gaussian Naive Bayes
ml.model.gaussian_nb.description: Each feature a bell curve per class, taken as independent: very fast.
ml.model.multinomial_nb.name: Multinomial Naive Bayes
ml.model.multinomial_nb.description: Counts per class, for non-negative inputs (inputs are scaled to [0, 1]).
ml.model.complement_nb.name: Complement Naive Bayes
ml.model.complement_nb.description: Multinomial Naive Bayes made robust to imbalanced classes.
ml.model.bernoulli_nb.name: Bernoulli Naive Bayes
ml.model.bernoulli_nb.description: Yes / no features per class (numbers are cut at 0 after standardising).
ml.model.mlp.name: Neural network (MLP)
ml.model.mlp.description: Layers of neurons that learn curved relations between the features.
ml.model.kernel_ridge.name: Kernel ridge
ml.model.kernel_ridge.description: A ridge regression through a kernel: smooth curves on small data.
ml.model.gaussian_process.name: Gaussian process
ml.model.gaussian_process.description: A distribution over smooth functions, with honest uncertainty: small data only.
ml.model.decision_tree.name: Decision tree
ml.model.decision_tree.description: Questions on one feature at a time, drawn as a tree: easy to read.
ml.model.extra_tree.name: Extra tree
ml.model.extra_tree.description: A single tree with random cut points: rarely used alone.
ml.model.random_forest.name: Random forest
ml.model.random_forest.description: Hundreds of trees on random rows and features, averaged: robust and accurate.
ml.model.extra_trees.name: Extra trees
ml.model.extra_trees.description: A random forest with random cut points: faster, often as accurate.
ml.model.bagging.name: Bagging
ml.model.bagging.description: Many full trees, each on a random draw of rows, averaged.
ml.model.hist_gradient_boosting.name: Histogram gradient boosting
ml.model.hist_gradient_boosting.descript: Many small trees, each correcting the previous ones, on binned features: fast on large data.
ml.model.gradient_boosting.name: Gradient boosting
ml.model.gradient_boosting.description: The classic boosting of shallow trees: accurate, slower than the histogram version.
ml.model.adaboost.name: AdaBoost
ml.model.adaboost.description: Each new tree focuses on the rows the previous ones got wrong.
ml.model.xgboost.name: XGBoost
ml.model.xgboost.description: Many small trees correcting each other, with regularization: the reference on tabular data.
ml.model.lightgbm.name: LightGBM
ml.model.lightgbm.description: Boosting that grows trees leaf by leaf: very fast on large data.
ml.model.catboost.name: CatBoost
ml.model.catboost.description: Boosting with symmetric trees, robust with little tuning.
ml.model.constant.name: Constant
ml.model.ensemble.name: Ensemble
ml.setting.regularization.label: Regularization
ml.setting.regularization.why: None keeps the coefficients readable, with standard errors and p-values.
ml.setting.alpha.label: Strength
ml.setting.alpha.why: 1 is a moderate penalty on standardised inputs.
ml.setting.alpha.why#2: A tiny L2 penalty for stability.
ml.setting.alpha.why#3: No penalty: the plain quantile regression.
ml.setting.alpha.why#5: The library's default for stochastic gradient descent.
ml.setting.alpha.why#6: Laplace smoothing: a category never seen in a class is not impossible.
ml.setting.alpha.why#7: A light L2 penalty on the weights.
ml.setting.l1_ratio.label: L1 share
ml.setting.fit_intercept.label: Intercept
ml.setting.fit_intercept.why: A constant term, almost always wanted.
ml.setting.solver.label: Solver
ml.setting.solver.why: Auto picks the exact method for the data.
ml.setting.solver.why#3: L-BFGS: fast and exact for L2.
ml.setting.solver.why#5: Adam adapts the step of each weight: robust default.
ml.setting.max_iter.label: Max iterations
ml.setting.max_iter.why: Enough to converge on most data.
ml.setting.max_iter.why#2: Enough to converge on standardised inputs.
ml.setting.max_iter.why#3: 300, cut short by early stopping on 10 % of the training rows.
ml.setting.tol.label: Tolerance
ml.setting.tol.why: Stops when an iteration improves less than this.
ml.setting.epsilon.label: Outlier threshold
ml.setting.epsilon.why: 1.35 keeps 95 % efficiency on normal errors while resisting outliers.
ml.setting.epsilon.why#2: Errors smaller than ε cost nothing (on the target's scale).
ml.setting.quantile.label: Quantile predicted
ml.setting.quantile.why: 0.5 predicts the median: robust to extreme values.
ml.setting.power.label: Power
ml.setting.power.why: Between 1 (Poisson) and 2 (Gamma): amounts with exact zeros.
ml.setting.C.label: C (penalty of errors)
ml.setting.C.why: C = 1 is the usual moderate penalty; lower C = simpler model.
ml.setting.C.why#2: 1 balances a smooth frontier and few training errors.
ml.setting.class_weight.label: Balance classes
ml.setting.class_weight.why#2: The rarest class is {share} of rows: weights balance it.
ml.setting.penalty.label: Penalty
ml.setting.penalty.why: L2 shrinks every weight a little and keeps them all.
ml.setting.penalty.why#2: L2 shrinks every weight a little.
ml.setting.multiclass.label: Multiclass strategy
ml.setting.multiclass.why: One model of all the classes together.
ml.setting.intercept_scaling.label: Intercept scaling
ml.setting.random_state.label: Seed
ml.setting.random_state.why: Fixed so that training again gives the same model.
ml.setting.loss.label: Loss
ml.setting.loss.why: Squared error for numbers; log loss gives probabilities.
ml.setting.learning_rate.label: Learning rate
ml.setting.learning_rate.why: The library's default for the problem.
ml.setting.learning_rate.why#2: 0.1: the usual balance of speed and accuracy.
ml.setting.eta0.label: Initial rate
ml.setting.eta0.why: Used by the constant, invscaling and adaptive schedules.
ml.setting.power_t.label: Power
ml.setting.power_t.why: How fast invscaling lowers the rate.
ml.setting.average.label: Averaging (ASGD)
ml.setting.average.why: Averaging the weights smooths the noise of stochastic steps.
ml.setting.early_stopping.label: Early stopping
ml.setting.early_stopping.why: Stops on 10 % of the training rows held out (never the test rows).
ml.setting.early_stopping.why#2: Stops when 10 % of the training rows held out stop improving (not the test rows).
ml.setting.early_stopping.why#3: Held-out 10 % of the training rows, never the test rows.
ml.setting.shrinkage.label: Shrinkage
ml.setting.shrinkage.why: Stabilises the covariance estimate with many inputs.
ml.setting.reg_param.label: Regularization
ml.setting.reg_param.why: Shrinks each class covariance towards the identity: QDA overfits easily.
ml.setting.n_neighbors.label: Neighbours k
ml.setting.n_neighbors.why#2: √n bounded to 5 to 50, odd for two classes: k = {k}.
ml.setting.weights.label: Weights
ml.setting.metric.label: Distance
ml.setting.p.label: Minkowski p
ml.setting.algorithm.label: Search
ml.setting.algorithm.why: Auto picks the fastest index for the data.
ml.setting.kernel.label: Kernel
ml.setting.kernel.why: RBF bends the frontier smoothly: the usual first choice.
ml.setting.gamma.label: γ (reach of each point)
ml.setting.degree.label: Degree
ml.setting.coef0.label: Kernel offset
ml.setting.cache_size.label: Cache (MB)
ml.setting.cache_size.why: More memory for the kernel speeds training up.
ml.setting.shrinking.label: Shrinking heuristic
ml.setting.nu.label: ν (share of support vectors)
ml.setting.nu.why: Upper bound on training errors, lower bound on support vectors.
ml.setting.radius.label: Radius
ml.setting.bins.label: Bins per number
ml.setting.bins.why: Numbers are cut into 10 quantile bins: the model only counts categories.
ml.setting.var_smoothing.label: Variance smoothing
ml.setting.var_smoothing.why: A tiny share of the largest variance added for stability.
ml.setting.hidden_layer_sizes.label: Hidden layers
ml.setting.hidden_layer_sizes.why: Two layers, wide then narrow: enough for most tabular data.
ml.setting.activation.label: Activation
ml.setting.validation_fraction.label: Held-out share
ml.setting.batch_size.label: Batch size
ml.setting.learning_rate_init.label: Initial learning rate
ml.setting.momentum.label: Momentum
ml.setting.nesterovs_momentum.label: Nesterov
ml.setting.beta_1.label: β1
ml.setting.beta_2.label: β2
ml.setting.n_iter_no_change.label: Patience (epochs)
ml.setting.n_iter_no_change.why: Trees without improvement before stopping (0 = never).
ml.setting.n_restarts_optimizer.label: Restarts of the kernel optimizer
ml.setting.n_restarts_optimizer.why: L-BFGS-B fits the kernel; restarts avoid local optima at a cost.
ml.setting.max_depth.label: Tree depth
ml.setting.max_depth.why#2: Unlimited: each tree grows until its leaves are small (0 = unlimited)
ml.setting.max_depth.why#3: Shallow trees, each correcting the previous ones.
ml.setting.min_samples_leaf.label: Min. rows per leaf
ml.setting.min_samples_leaf.why: 20 avoids leaves built on a handful of rows.
ml.setting.criterion.label: Split quality
ml.setting.splitter.label: Splitter
ml.setting.ccp_alpha.label: Pruning (ccp α)
ml.setting.n_estimators.label: Number of trees
ml.setting.n_estimators.why: 300 trees: more rarely helps, it only costs time.
ml.setting.n_estimators.why#2: 100 trees in the browser version, on one core (R-WEB-02); 300 in the desktop app.
ml.setting.n_estimators.why#3: 50 full trees, each on a random draw of rows.
ml.setting.n_estimators.why#4: 200 small trees, cut short when 10 % held-out rows stop improving.
ml.setting.n_estimators.why#5: 1 000, cut short by early stopping: it finds the right number.
ml.setting.max_features.label: Features tried per split
ml.setting.max_features.why: The library's default for the problem.
ml.setting.bootstrap.label: Bootstrap rows
ml.setting.bootstrap.why: Each tree sees a random draw of the rows.
ml.setting.max_samples.label: Rows per tree
ml.setting.max_leaf_nodes.label: Max leaves per tree
ml.setting.l2_regularization.label: L2 penalty
ml.setting.max_bins.label: Max bins
ml.setting.monotonic.label: Monotonic constraints
ml.setting.monotonic.why: Optional, e.g. “size:+1, age:-1”: the prediction may only rise with size and only fall with age (business knowledge the model must respect).
ml.setting.subsample.label: Rows per tree
ml.setting.base_depth.label: Depth of each tree
ml.setting.base_depth.why: Stumps for classes, depth 3 for numbers.
ml.setting.colsample_bytree.label: Features per tree
ml.setting.min_child_weight.label: Min. weight per leaf
ml.setting.reg_lambda.label: L2 penalty
ml.setting.reg_alpha.label: L1 penalty
ml.setting.patience.label: Early stopping patience
ml.setting.booster.label: Booster
ml.setting.tree_method.label: Tree construction
ml.setting.max_bin.label: Max bins
ml.setting.num_leaves.label: Number of leaves
ml.setting.min_child_samples.label: Min. rows per leaf
ml.setting.boosting_type.label: Boosting
ml.setting.iterations.label: Iterations
ml.setting.depth.label: Depth
ml.setting.l2_leaf_reg.label: L2 penalty
ml.setting.border_count.label: Borders per feature
ml.badge.slow_to_predict_on_this_data: Slow to predict on this data
ml.recommend.small_data_a_simple_model_i: Small data: a simple model is hard to beat.
ml.recommend.many_categories_or_empty_ce: Many categories or empty cells: boosting handles them well.
ml.recommend.readable_every_weight_can_b: Readable: every weight can be explained.
ml.recommend.large_data_boosting_is_accu: Large data: boosting is accurate and fast.
ml.recommend.large_data_a_linear_model_f: Large data: a linear model fitted a few rows at a time.
ml.ruleReason.l1_penalty_needs_the_libli: L1 penalty needs the liblinear or saga solver.
ml.ruleReason.elastic_net_needs_the_saga: Elastic net needs the saga solver.
ml.ruleReason.liblinear_always_penalises: liblinear always penalises: choose another solver.
ml.ruleReason.cosine_distance_only_works: Cosine distance only works with brute-force search.
ml.ruleReason.l_bfgs_has_no_early_stoppi: L-BFGS has no early stopping: it uses all the training rows at once.
ml.limit.kernel_svm: Kernel SVMs need ≤ {rows} training rows (their cost grows with the square of the rows).
ml.limit.kernel_ridge: Kernel ridge needs ≤ {rows} training rows (its cost grows with the cube of the rows).
ml.limit.gaussian_process: A Gaussian process needs ≤ {rows} training rows (its cost grows with the cube of the rows).
